instruction: Look at bore_plate.step in SOLIDWORKS with the SOLIDWORKS CAM add-in. At the start of the task, start SOLIDWORKS 2025 from the desktop shortcut and use its installed SOLIDWORKS CAM/CAMWorks add-in; there is no separate SolidCAM desktop program in this image. Spot drill and drill the four through holes in bore_plate.step. Machine the two stepped holes using Bore, Profile, or Pocket operations. Through holes must break through the bottom by 1 mm and stepped holes must bottom at Z=9.000 mm. Use standard Drill plus Bore, Pocket, Profile, or Contour operations for the stepped-hole machining, and keep SOLIDWORKS CAM's default generated NC comments; do not rename operations just to add labels. Do not force exact tool station numbers, spindle speeds, feedrates, or internal tool-library IDs if SOLIDWORKS CAM's Technology Database assigns stable defaults; use suitable installed tool-library entries for the required operation types and let the posted NC program reflect those real CAM selections. Save the required output file(s) to the Desktop: C:\Users\User\Desktop\task-8.nc. Generate the required NC/G-code file(s) by using SOLIDWORKS CAM's normal Post Process workflow after calculating the toolpath, with an installed .ctl postprocessor from C:\ProgramData\SOLIDWORKS\SOLIDWORKS CAM 2025\Posts. For milling tasks, prefer m3axis-tutorial.ctl, mach_iii.ctl, or haas_vf3.ctl; for turning tasks, use an installed turning .ctl post such as fanuc_t2axis.ctl. If the generated program opens in NC Editor or is initially saved with a different extension, use Save As from that generated program to save the exact requested Desktop filename(s).
source: SolidCAM 模块总览含 2.5D Milling、AFRM、Turning、Mill-Turn 等模块：https://solidcam.com/cam-modules/modules-overview/ (SolidCAM)
